messages:
dave_acme: Hey, we're seeing intermittent TLS failures to our private endpoint after you rotated certs last night. About 20% of requests from our users get a handshake error 525. No app code changes on our side.

alice_support: Thanks for reporting — sorry for the trouble. Can you paste the exact error and a short curl/openssl test you ran? Also which VPC region and VIP?

dave_acme: Region eu-west-1, VIP 10.100.5.12. Error in our logs:
```
Error: TLS handshake failed: remote error: tls: bad certificate
  at https://api.private.acme.example/v1/foo
```
I ran `openssl s_client -connect 10.100.5.12:443 -servername api.private.acme.example -showcerts` intermittently and sometimes the server returns just the leaf cert (no intermediate). Other times it returns full chain.

alice_support: Huh. That sounds like a partial-chain being served by the proxy intermittently. Can you share two outputs (one bad, one good)? Blur any serials.

dave_acme: Pasted (trimmed):
--- bad ---
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIF...LEAF...
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
--- no additional certs ---
```
--- good ---
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIF...LEAF...
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIE...INTERMEDIATE...
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIJ...ROOT...
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
```

alice_support: Thanks. I'm escalating to SRE/eng. @bob_sre @carol_eng can you take a look? We're seeing intermittent chain trimming on the private VIP after the rotator ran last night; customer observes correlation with OCSP timeouts.

bob_sre: Investigating. First hypothesis: when our rotator tries to staple OCSP and the OCSP responder times out due to egress allowlist, the proxy path may drop intermediate certs to reduce handshake time. Looking for rotator logs for that window (1749950000-1749960000).

rotator_bot: rotator: completed rotation for tenant acme-corp at 2024-11-08T22:30:12Z status=success; ocsp_fetch=timeout_retry; uploaded_bundle_size=3

carol_eng: Interesting — rotator reports ocsp_fetch=timeout_retry but upload_bundle_size=3 (bundle included leaf+intermediate+root). Proxy should serve full bundle. Do we have HAProxy/Envoy config that prunes chain on OCSP failure?

bob_sre: On the proxy side, we have a small optimization that will attempt to fetch stapled OCSP and, if it can't get a stapled response within 800ms, we fast-path the handshake without stapling. There's also a legacy codepath that inadvertently serves only the leaf when KV cache reloads concurrently. I'm reproducing locally.

carol_eng: Can you share the repro steps? We need to confirm it's a race during hot reloads.

bob_sre: Repro steps I used (quick):
1) spin up envoy with our 1.14 config and load initial cert bundle (leaf+int+root)
2) trigger cert reload via POST to /admin/reload while blocking egress to ocsp.int-ca.example for 1s (iptables DROP)
3) run a loop of `openssl s_client -connect vip:443 -servername host -showcerts`
Observed ~15% of connections returned only leaf cert. Logs show `cert_chain_write: partial_bundle_served due_to_atomic_swap` at reload time.

carol_eng: Nice repro, thanks. That log string is from an older branch — I pushed a fix for atomic swap ordering in config reloads last quarter but it didn't make it into the 1.14 build we rolled in that region. We can do either: rollback rotation to previous bundle, or hot-patch proxy to ensure atomic full-bundle publish. Which is preferable for acme-corp?

alice_support: Customer prefers minimum downtime. They'd accept a hot-patch if we can roll it quickly and verify.

dave_acme: Hot-patch is fine as long as you can do it without rolling traffic away from our VIP for too long. We're seeing user impact now.

bob_sre: Plan: patch envoy/ha proxy binary with the atomic-swap reorder fix, deploy to a small canary group of hosts in eu-west-1, monitor for `partial_bundle_served` logs and TLS handshake errors (metric tls.handshakes.failed). If canary looks good, roll to remaining hosts. ETA ~ 90m. I'll also open egress rule check with customer to ensure OCSP host is allowed (this reduces timeout noise).

carol_eng: Also adding a server-side guard: if rotator's ocsp_fetch times out, still accept and serve the full uploaded bundle instead of pruning. Small rotator change -> 1-line guard. I'll prepare a PR and cherry-pick to the rotator release branch.

alice_support: Thanks team. @dave_acme we'll update you as we start the canary deploy and once the rotator patch lands. Can you confirm whether your VPC egress ACL allows outbound to ocsp.int-ca.example:80/443? If not, can you allow it during the next 2 hours while we validate?

dave_acme: Our egress was on a deny-by-default list. I've added a temporary allow to ocsp.int-ca.example:443 and will keep it for 2h.

tls_mon_bot: ALERT: tls.handshakes.failed for tenant acme-corp -> decreased by 87% since 1749999400 (canary start).

bob_sre: Canary looks good: no `partial_bundle_served` in canary logs and handshake failures down to baseline. Rolling to rest of hosts now.

alice_support: Rolling complete. Can you confirm your users are seeing normal behavior?

dave_acme: Confirmed. No more 525s from our side in the last 10 minutes. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

carol_eng: We'll backport the rotator guard and schedule a follow-up patch to remove the legacy prune path. I'll file the PR and link here shortly.

alice_support: Closing this thread once PR is merged and customer confirms. Thanks all. :pray:
